Theorem F.3.9 (Proved: holomorphic periods on every open base). Let B be
an open connected Riemann surface and ρ : π1 (B) → GL+ (6, R) any representation. Its
associated flat D3 -bundle admits a holomorphic section. More generally, every continuous
section which is holomorphic near a compact Runge set can be deformed through sections
to a holomorphic section, with arbitrary uniform approximation there and any prescribed
finite-order interpolation at finitely many points of that set. For an integral representation,
this gives a holomorphic family of complex three-tori with the prescribed lattice local system
and a zero section over B.

Proof. The flat bundle D = B  e ×ρ D3 → B is a holomorphic fibre bundle: its transition maps
are constant real linear transformations, acting holomorphically on the Grassmannian. Its
fibre has LSAP by Theorem F.3.8, so the bundle map is an Oka–1 map by [AF25, Proposition
7.13(d)]. The lifting property in Definition 7.7 of that paper, applied to the identity map of
B, gives precisely the stated section deformation and approximation, including the finite jets.
This uses the section theorem, rather than an inference from the Oka–1 property for maps to
the fibre alone.



                                                305
    There is a continuous section to start with. An open Riemann surface has the homotopy
type of a one-dimensional CW complex; a bundle with connected fibre admits a section
over its vertices and edges, and the homotopy lifting property transports this section to B.
Connectedness holds for the chosen component D3 . Taking the Runge set empty therefore
proves existence.
    For an integral representation let VZ be its lattice local system and let F ⊂ VZ ⊗ OB
be the resulting holomorphic rank-three subbundle. Real transversality says that projection
identifies the real vector bundle with the underlying real bundle of Q = (VZ ⊗ OB )/F. Hence
the image of VZ is a full lattice in every fibre of Q. Locally it is uniformly discrete and
acts by holomorphic translations. The quotient Q/VZ → B is consequently a smooth proper
holomorphic family of compact complex three-tori, with its evident zero section and the
required marking.

Scope of F.3.8–F.3.9. Taking B = P1 \{singular values} settles existence of nondegenerate
holomorphic periods on the smooth locus for every oriented rank-six datum. It does not impose
good reduction after the finite root changes or the bounded correction to the logarithmic cusp
period. Those are conditions at points missing from B, whereas the interpolation theorem
controls only finite jets at points lying in B. Exact agreement with a prescribed germ on an
annulus cannot be requested either: the identity theorem would then determine its analytic
continuation. Thus this theorem advances the unrestricted F.3 problem but does not decide
all its compactification conditions.

Lemma F.3.10 (Proved: retaining isolated extension points). Let R be an open
Riemann surface, V → R a holomorphic vector bundle, and U ⊂ Grr (V ) an open subset
whose projection onto R is surjective. Let S ⊂ R be finite. Suppose that over R \ S this
projection is a holomorphic fibre bundle with an LSAP fibre. Let K ⊂ R be a compact
Runge set containing S in its interior. Every continuous section of U which is holomorphic
near K can be deformed through sections to a holomorphic section, with arbitrary uniform
approximation on K and interpolation of any given finite jets at finitely many points of its
interior. No fibre-bundle or Serre-fibration assertion is required at the points of S.

Proof. Here are the details of the relative version of the LSAP argument in [AF25, Lemma
5.1, Theorem 6.1 and Proposition 7.13(d)]. They also specify why isolated extension points
cause no new analytic step. Enlarge K slightly inside the domain of holomorphicity, retaining
the Runge property. Choose a strongly subharmonic Morse exhaustion of R starting with
this compact set. All subsequent boundary arcs, attached discs and critical one-handles can
and will be chosen disjoint from S. On them U is an ordinary holomorphic bundle with
LSAP fibre.
    The global spray on the old compact set can be taken to be vertical even though the
fibres at S differ. Indeed, let f be the current holomorphic section on a Stein neighborhood
W of that set. Put A equal to the finite interpolation set, including S, and choose an ideal
sheaf I vanishing to one more than the prescribed jet orders at its points. Cartan’s theorem
A supplies finitely many holomorphic sections T1 , . . . , TN of End(V )|W ⊗ I which generate
End(V ) on the compact attaching arcs, after shrinking W if needed. The formula
                                                           
                                                 N
                                F (z, a) = exp                                        (F.O5)
                                                X
                                                   aj Tj (z) f (z)
                                              j=1

defines a holomorphic spray of sections of the Grassmannian bundle. Its differential in
a surjects onto the vertical tangent space at every attaching point, since End(Vz ) →


                                             306
Hom(f (z), Vz /f (z)) is onto. For a sufficiently small it has range in U on a neighborhood of
the old compact set, by openness and compactness. Every parameter value preserves all the
chosen jets. Domination at A is neither asserted nor used.
    For a noncritical extension, subdivide the new annular regions into small discs lying in
bundle trivializations over R \ S. Restrict (F.O5) to a thin attaching disc. LSAP of the fibre
extends this spray across the attached disc, approximating the old spray as closely as desired
on the intersection. The spray gluing used in the proof of [AF25, Lemma 5.1, equations
(5.6)–(5.8)] now applies verbatim to vertical sprays: the inverse-function step is needed only
on the attaching intersection, where (F.O5) is dominating. It produces reparametrizations of
the two sprays and a glued section. The old part remains in U because it is evaluated in
(F.O5); the new part remains in U because the LSAP spray takes values in the bundle fibre.
The fixed jets survive the reparametrizations, being independent of the spray parameters on
the old side.
    For a critical extension, first extend over the attached real arc using the given continuous
section and the homotopy already constructed on the old compact set. Apply Mergelyan
approximation with the same finite jets to a neighborhood of the union of the old set and
this arc, and then apply the noncritical step. To see explicitly that this approximation is by
sections, trivialize V holomorphically on the open Riemann surface: its underlying complex
bundle is trivial over a graph spine, and the frame bundle therefore has a continuous section.
Its fibre GL(rank V, C) has the dominating spray (g, A) 7→ g exp A, so [FP02, Theorem 1.2]
gives a holomorphic frame. The section is then a map to the fixed Grassmannian, to which
[AF25, Theorem 2.13] applies. The base coordinate is kept unchanged. Close approximation
on the compact arc and old set, followed by shrinking its neighborhood, preserves membership
in the open subset U . This is the critical case of Theorem 6.1 of that paper, with no
approximation performed at a singular point of the projection: here the projection is a
submersion everywhere, as U is open in a Grassmannian bundle.
    Choose successive errors summably small on the preceding compact sets and smaller than
their distances to the complement of U . The sections converge uniformly on every compact
set to a holomorphic section with range in U . The finite jets persist. The close homotopies
on successive stages concatenate in the usual exhaustion construction. All new attachment
regions lie outside S; the old section remains holomorphic on a full neighborhood of each
point of S at every stage. This proves the lemma.

is a holomorphic period family with this monodromy and nondegenerate real transversality

For every fixed C0 , and uniformly for C in a sufficiently small bounded neighborhood of C0 ,
the matrix in (F.O7) is invertible with positive determinant when |t| is sufficiently small. This

    Start with a polynomial C0 (t) realizing the desired finite jet. Formula (F.O7) makes it
a holomorphic section on a small closed cusp disc K, which is Runge in B. This section
extends continuously over B. To justify the relative extension, D3 is connected and simply
connected: it retracts onto SO(6)/U (3), and π1 (U (3)) → π1 (SO(6)) is onto, since a unitary
rotation in one complex coordinate is a generator of the real two-plane rotation loop. A
cellular decomposition of the surface outside the cusp disc now extends its boundary section
over edges by connectedness and over two-cells by simple connectivity. The flat bundle is
trivial over each cell. This argument uses no fibration property at p0 .
    Over B \{p0 } the fibre is the LSAP manifold D3 from Theorem F.3.8. Lemma F.3.10, with
S = {p0 }, produces a holomorphic section of U over all of B, with the chosen jet at p0 . Since
its value at p0 lies in the affine chart just adjoined, it has a holomorphic matrix C(t) there.
Undoing the canonical frame gives exactly (F.O6), with a bounded holomorphic correction.
Everywhere else membership in U is precisely nondegeneracy of the complex-torus periods.
More explicitly, choose three members of a real lattice basis whose projected periods are
complex-linearly independent, and normalize them to I3 . The remaining three periods form a
matrix Z, and real transversality is exactly det Im Z 6= 0. This normalization persists locally.
A single Schubert chart is not imposed globally, and none is needed to define a marked torus
period family.
    For F.2 survivors, Theorem F.2.7 excludes k = 3 and Proposition F.2.15 proves orientation
preservation of the finite matrices for k = 2. The cusp determinant is also one. Thus all
survivors satisfy the hypotheses. This is a universal existence decision and does not require
completion of their simultaneous integral classification.

Finite good reduction remains a distinct requirement. Theorem F.3.11 resolves
the period-existence clause of F.3 as written: its base is the punctured sphere, and its
specified end condition is the bounded cusp correction. It does not claim that every such
family extends at the other punctures after the finite root changes. Requiring that stronger
simultaneous extension would retain every puncture and leave a compact base, to which the
Runge exhaustion used above does not apply. The specific compact fourfold in F.4 already
has all its finite extensions by Theorems F.3.5–F.3.7; its existence does not depend on this
stronger unresolved general compactification question.

6.2   The oriented smooth type
Theorem F.4.1 (Proved: a complex structure on the stated connected sum). The
compact complex fourfold of Theorem F.3.7 is three-connected, has Euler number six, and is
orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic to

                                        3HP2 # (−HP2 ).                                     (F.25)

Its integral middle lattice is I3,1 and, in a diagonal integral basis, p1 /2 = (1, 1, 1, 1). In
particular the conclusion is an exact smooth diffeomorphism, with no remaining homotopy-
sphere ambiguity.

Proof. Theorem F.2.6 gives three-connectivity and free integral homology with middle rank
four. The complex orientation and Theorem F.1.2 give signature two, the odd unimodular
form I3,1 , and c22 = 2. Since H 2 = 0, we have c1 = 0 and p1 = −2c2 . The reduction of c2
modulo two is w4 . The Wu formula, with w1 = w2 = 0, says that w4 is characteristic for the
middle form. Thus v = p1 /2 = −c2 is characteristic and v 2 = 2. It is primitive: a nontrivial
integral divisor would have square dividing two. This excludes every divisor of absolute value
at least two.
    We verify the orbit of this vector in L = I3,1 . Its orthogonal complement K = v ⊥ is even,
indefinite of signature (2, 1), with determinant of absolute value two. Unimodularity of L and
primitivity of v give w ∈ L with (w, v) = 1. The vector k = w − v/2 represents the nonzero
element of K ∗ /K ≃ Z/2. Its discriminant square is
                                             1   1
                                 k2 = w2 −     ≡      (mod 2Z),                             (F.26)
                                             2   2
because characteristicity makes w2 odd. Consequently K has the signature and discriminant
form of U ⊕ h2i, hence the same genus by [Nik80, Corollary 1.9.4]. Nikulin’s Theorem 1.14.2
applies: the rank is three, the odd-primary discriminant lengths are zero, and the two-primary
length is one, so its additional equality-case condition at two does not arise. The genus
has a single isomorphism class. Thus K ≃ U ⊕ h2i. The extension from Zv ⊕ K to the
odd unimodular lattice L has index two. Its gluing subgroup is the unique nontrivial graph
between the two discriminant groups of order two. Every isomorphism of complements
therefore extends, taking v to a chosen characteristic vector of square two. The vector
(1, 1, 1, 1) is such a vector in I3,1 . This proves the asserted orbit, including the class of p1 .
     Let M = 3HP2 #(−HP2 ) with the      Pdisplayed orientation. Its intersection form is I3,1 , and
its standard generators have p1 = 2 i xi , as used and derived in Theorem F.1.3. Therefore
the two manifolds have isomorphic middle forms and first Pontryagin classes. These determine
Wall’s full normal invariant in dimension eight. Indeed the normal rank-four bundle of a
representative embedded S 4 has Euler number its self-intersection and Pontryagin number the
evaluation of p1 (T M ), since p1 (T S 4 ) = 0. The clutching group is π3 Spin(4) = Z ⊕ Z; with
compatible generators (a, b) its two characteristic numbers are e = a − b and p1 = −2(a + b).
This pair is injective, so no additional unstable normal invariant is omitted.
     Wall’s classification theorem in the precise formulation [BHS19b, Recollection 2.2,
Definition 2.5 and Theorem 2.6] now gives an oriented diffeomorphism after connected sum
with some Σ ∈ Θ8 . We remove this ambiguity using the exact inertia calculation [Nag26,
Theorem 1.4 and its proof in Section 9]: for a closed three-connected eight-manifold its
inertia group is zero exactly when p1 is divisible by eight; otherwise, since Θ8 = Z/2, it is
all of Θ8 . Here p1 has divisibility two. Thus M #Σ is oriented diffeomorphic to M for both
possibilities for Σ. This proves (F.25).



                                                309
    The application of Nagy’s theorem uses the published 2026 paper by Csaba Nagy, whose
theorem and proof were opened in this run; it is not an inference from the earlier announcement
with Crowley. Mandal’s almost-complex criterion alone gives no integrability statement. Here
integrability comes from the periods and the compact charts of Theorems F.3.5–F.3.7, while
the cited classification results identify their smooth manifold.

Conclusion F.2.4 (Proved: resolution of the classification problem). The previously
incomplete linear classification and all-twist integral topology computation are completed by
F.2.31 and F.2.35–39, with the fixed cusp filling and full marking specified as required by
F.2.3. Every linear tuple has an exact canonical representative and a returned unimodular
conjugator; the finite bound depends on the supplied input. The unbounded trace family
proves that no fixed global height cutoff can replace this procedure. All actual affine orders,
numerators, clutch vectors and cusp markings are included in the general fundamental-group
and integral homology algorithms. The complete constructive survivor list, its integral tests
and the common oriented smooth type are given in F.2.30.
    This conclusion does not claim an executed enumeration of the infinite general class
set. The exhaustive finite involution catalogue, the general comparison tests, the three full
topology integrations and the unified wrapper checks have the exact executed scopes stated
in F.2.35–39. The earlier obstruction record is retained verbatim in records/fourfolds_F2
_4_superseded.tex; its finite-order filter and homology-level obstructions were superseded
by the complete canonical and chain constructions.

Conclusion F.3.3 (Proved: the previously open period decision). Theorem F.3.11
now gives a positive answer for every topological survivor of F.2: there is a holomorphic
period family on the punctured sphere, with nondegenerate imaginary part in every local
normalized period chart and a bounded holomorphic correction at its primitive maximal
cusp. The proof is universal and does not require that the remaining integral classification
be finite. The proposed polarized abelian-surface source is excluded by Theorem F.3.4; the
universal construction instead uses the explicit unpolarized LSAP domain and the relative
section principle in F.3.8–F.3.11. Simultaneous good reduction at every finite puncture is a
stronger compactification condition than the literal F.3 statement and is not inferred from
this argument. It is already proved for the explicit compact fourfold of F.4.
